claims.text: 8 out of 12 reviewed studies concluded that racial bias was present in clinical machine learning models.
2 out of 12 reviewed studies concluded that racial bias was not present in the evaluated clinical machine learning models.
All 8 reviewed studies that implemented mitigation methods successfully increased algorithmic fairness based on their chosen metrics.
Preprocessing was the most commonly used bias mitigation strategy among the reviewed clinical machine learning studies.
Convolutional neural networks were the most frequent machine learning modeling technique used across the reviewed studies.
Equal opportunity difference was the most commonly observed fairness metric used to evaluate racial bias in the reviewed literature.
In-processing bias mitigation methods were ineffective in reducing bias and were outperformed by other mitigation strategies in the reviewed studies.

evidence.description: In addition, 8 (67%) studies concluded that racial bias was present, 2 (17%) concluded that it was not.
All 8 (67%) studies that implemented methods for mitigation of racial bias successfully increased fairness, as measured by the authors' chosen metrics.
Preprocessing bias mitigation was the most commonly used strategy (7/13, 54%).
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were the predominant ML modeling technique used (5/12, 42%).
The most commonly observed metrics were equal opportunity difference (5/12, 42%), accuracy (4/12, 25%), and disparate impact (2/12, 17%).
However, in both studies, in-processing was ineffective in reducing bias and was outperformed by other bias mitigation methods.

methodologies.name: PRISMA-guided Scoping Review
methodologies.description: A scoping review conducted following PRISMA guidelines to systematically screen and synthesize literature on racial bias assessment and mitigation in clinical machine learning models.
conditions: Development or evaluation of a clinically relevant ML model
Evaluation of model bias regarding racial or ethnic groups

limitations.text: The search strategy may have overlooked relevant publications due to the heterogeneity of terminology used to describe machine learning and racial bias.
The review was limited by publication bias as non-full-length manuscripts were excluded and studies finding no racial bias may be less likely to be published.
The paucity of literature and lack of standardized methods to evaluate and mitigate bias precluded performing a meta-analysis or systematic review.
Adoption of algorithmic fairness principles in medicine remains limited by poor data availability and inconsistent machine learning model reporting.

future_work.text: Further research is needed to establish standardized best practices for fairness evaluation and bias mitigation in clinical machine learning.
Researchers and journal editors should emphasize standardized reporting guidelines and data availability in medical ML studies to improve transparency.
